item.description:
Remind Me brings a session back, and file tabs become windows

Wortel 2026.47.1 · 2026-11-17

Remind Me. Some sessions you want to come back to later, not now. Choose Remind Me from a session’s menu or the Session menu (⌘P finds it too), then In 30 Minutes, In 1 Hour, In 3 Hours, Tomorrow at 09:00, Monday at 09:00 or Custom… for a day and time of your own. While it waits, the row says when on the small grey line under its name. When the time comes, the session gets the unread ring and a banner, or only a flash of the ring if you’re already looking at it. A reminder that came due while Wortel was closed goes off when you open it. Closing a session ends its reminder. From a terminal, wortel remind 20m, wortel remind fri 9am or wortel remind none does the same. Usage data now counts that a reminder was set, with nothing about the session or the time.

File tabs and windows. A file tab dragged past the edge of the window becomes a preview window where you let it go, as Safari’s tabs do. Drag a preview window by its top row onto a tab row and it becomes a tab again, keeping its diff and its view. Preview windows now look like Wortel’s main window, with the file’s name and Diff · Source · Rendered in the top row.

Files open in the main area. A file opened from the Files pane, Changes, History or a link in a terminal went to the narrow side column. It now opens in the main area until you drag one elsewhere, and that session remembers. Hold ⌥ to open it in the other place.

Fixes. ⌘J, ⇧⌘T, ⌘F and ⌘G typed into the program when a terminal was focused; they reach the menu again. Grabbing a tab just after opening a file sometimes moved the whole window instead. Folded folders in the sidebar now stack close together. A Markdown file with front matter rendered it as a huge heading; it now shows as a block of YAML.

Scroll and select in Codex after reopening Wortel

Wortel 2026.46.6 · 2026-11-12

Scrolling and selecting in Codex. Codex fills the whole terminal and does its own scrolling and selecting, so when it starts it asks the terminal to pass the mouse on. When Wortel started Codex again in a session you weren’t looking at, a long conversation could push that request out of what Wortel keeps for a session while you’re away. Opening the session then gave you a terminal that had never been asked, and the mouse did nothing. Wortel now notes those requests on their way out and repeats them when the session comes back. This takes effect once the process that keeps your terminals running has started afresh: close your sessions and quit Wortel for half a minute, or restart your Mac.

⌘C copies what Codex selected. With a selection Codex drew itself, ⌘C did nothing: Wortel’s Copy command took the key and found nothing selected in the terminal. The key now goes on to the program when the terminal has no selection of its own. Copying text you selected in the terminal works as before.

Smaller things. An image smaller than the side column no longer pulls its tab’s header down to the middle of the column; the picture is centred at its own size. A file that isn’t text no longer offers Diff and Source in its tab, where both showed the same picture.

Screen readers can read the terminal

Wortel 2026.46.5 · 2026-11-12

Screen readers can read the terminal. Apps that read text aloud or describe the screen, like VoiceOver, ask macOS what an app is showing. Until now Wortel’s terminal told them nothing. It now answers as a text area: they get the text on screen (also after you scroll back), the text you’ve selected with a drag, and where every word sits, so a read-aloud app can highlight each word as it speaks it. They’re told when the screen changes, a few times a second at most, and none of this costs anything until an app asks.

Send Feedback. Help ▸ Send Feedback… opens an email to hello@wortel.sh with your Wortel version, macOS version and your Mac’s chip already filled in, so you can see everything in it before you send.

Better crash reports, less location. If you share anonymous usage data, Wortel now notes whether its last run ended cleanly or crashed, and after a crash it sends where in Wortel’s own code that happened, as numbers only, with no file paths or names. It also counts which agents you start, from a fixed list, and how often sessions are archived. Usage data no longer includes a location looked up from your internet address.
